zh.title: OpenAI Dots来了：AI越来越能干，我能少操点心了吗？
zh.excerpt: 真正让人轻松的，不是 AI 多做几件事，而是它能持续推进、懂得边界，让一件反复挂念的工作真正被交出去。
zh.content:
![OpenAI Dots、GPT-6.1 Sol 与 Agent 工作方式的变化](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/source-poster.png)

你有没有发现，用 AI 工作，有时很像带一个特别聪明、但需要不断喊“继续”的同事。

方案写得很好。然后呢？你来。

资料查了一堆。谁判断哪条可信？你来。

任务做到一半停住了。谁记得明天接着推进？还是你。

一天下来，内容多了，窗口多了，待办也多了。你本来想找个帮手，结果给自己新增了一个岗位：AI 项目经理。

今天，我在「虾子曰·昨日世界」看到 OpenAI Dots 的海报，又顺着线索看了官方资料。我最在意的，是它能不能帮我们少一点这样的操心。

**把一件事交出去，也把一点时间还给自己。**

![AI 越来越能干，我能少操点心吗？](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/cover.png)

## 01｜Dots 想接走的，是“后面那一串事”

OpenAI 在这次 DevDay 推出的 Dots，是一种可以持续工作的智能体。官方把它描述为能承担长期任务、在两次对话之间继续推进事情的 Agent。[1]

你交给它一个目标，说明可以自行处理到哪里，再回来查看结果。

背后有几个支点：自己的云端电脑和浏览器、已连接的工具、持续上下文，以及把工作分给其他 Agent 的能力。[1][2] OpenAI 的系统卡明确写到，Dots 由 GPT-6 Astra 驱动。[2]

海报里同场出现的 GPT-6.1 Sol，是另一项模型更新。[7] 读这条新闻时，可以先把两件事分开：模型能力在进步，围绕模型的工作方式也在改变。

这让我想到很多互联网人的一天：上午看用户反馈，中午改产品，下午查数据，晚上准备内容。每件事单拿出来，AI 好像都能帮一点。可把它们串成一个真正向前走的项目，操心的仍然是你。

Dots 值得期待的地方，就在这些连接处。

它能不能记住事情推进到了哪一步？发现情况变了，能不能调整安排？遇到必须由人判断的分岔路，能不能带着清楚的选项回来？

> **会做一道题令人惊喜。能把一件事持续做好，才让人放心。**

![从一次回答，到持续推进一件事](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/ongoing-work.png)

## 02｜我更想拿它试试这种“小事”

比如，一个人做 App，最容易拖着不做的用户反馈整理。

你当然可以说：“帮我分析一下这些反馈。”然后收获一篇很像咨询报告的文章，读完点头，关掉，再也没打开。

我更想尝试这样的委托：

> 接下来七天，每天检查我授权的反馈表。把重复问题归类，附上原话和来源；周五交付最值得改的三个问题，以及判断依据。先只读和整理，不联系用户，不改线上产品；遇到信息不足，标出来。

这是我设想的试用任务，还不是 Dots 的实测结果。

它的价值很好验收：周五到底有没有交东西？来源对不对？昨天指出的误判，今天有没有修正？

真正省下来的，可能不只是整理表格的二十分钟。还有洗澡时突然想起“糟了，那些反馈还没看”的那一下。

**有些工作最累的部分，是一直挂在脑子里。**

对一个人做产品的人来说，如果能放心交出去一件反复发生的事，就已经很有价值。没必要一上来，就让 AI 替你经营整家公司。

## 03｜那它和 Muse、Cue 有什么不同？

先说一个容易误会的地方：持续执行并非 Dots 独有。

Meta 在 Muse 的官方介绍中，同样强调了关闭 App 后继续工作、记住长期目标，以及跨应用办事。[3]

三家都在往“把事情做下去”走。下面的比较，是我从官方材料中读到的产品重心，不是同场实测排名。

![三种产品重心，同一个方向：把事情做下去](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/three-agents.png)

**Dots：把持续委托放进 ChatGPT。**

它把对话、已连接的工作资料和后续任务放在同一条关系里。我会优先用它试验那些需要几天推进、反复检查的工作，观察自己究竟少催了几次。

**Muse：从个人生活，伸进小生意。**

9 月 29 日，Meta 又发布了 Muse for Small Business，连接 Shopify、Stripe、Slack、Notion 等工具，以及 Facebook、Instagram 商家账号，帮助分析经营情况、准备营销内容。它已不只是“帮你订个旅行”的生活助手。[4]

我的理解是，它想接住那些已经在开店、经营账号的人：你照顾眼前的顾客，AI 帮你处理后台的一部分琐事。

**Cue：给 Agent 一个能与外界打交道的身份。**

Manus 为 Cue 突出的，是 Agent 自己的邮箱、电话号码、钱包和电脑，还能把多个 Agent 放进群聊协作。付款受你设定的预算约束；这里的钱包不能被理解为一个可随意支配的不受限银行账户。[5]

一个比较具体的区别是：Dots 首发文档说，它可以连接你的个人邮箱，但暂时不能拥有自己的独立邮箱，也不能主动打电话给你。Cue 则把独立身份摆在了台前。[1]

Dots 让我想到持续跟进，Muse 让我想到已有生意，Cue 让我想到对外协作。

它们的能力有重叠，最终哪一个适合你，还是要看你的任务、工具和授权方式。

## 04｜能干之外，我更在意它“懂不懂停”

试想一下，你只说“帮我看看下周怎么推广”，AI 就替你发出了广告、联系了客户、花掉了预算。

执行力很强。血压也很容易升高。

所以我看 Dots 的官方说明时，特别留意了一个区别：主动研究，与获准执行，是两回事。

OpenAI 说明，主动研究可以读取获准来源、整理信息，但这类研究工具不能直接发消息、修改插件中的内容或控制电脑；后续行动仍须遵循授权与检查。转账等敏感动作需要人接手，已完成的动作也不是都能撤销。[6]

Meta 对小企业版 Muse 也写得很直接：发布、发送、花费，都需要用户批准。[4]

这些细节会决定，我们敢不敢把它用进真实工作。

一个好的帮手，应该知道哪些事情自己往前做，哪些事情先等一下。你中途改主意，它得听得进去；卡住了，它得说清楚卡在哪里。

> **知道什么时候继续，也知道什么时候停下来。**

![把交付、权限和回来汇报的时机写清楚](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/boundaries.png)

如果准备试 Dots，我会先写清三件事：

1. **交付什么。** 给我一份带来源的候选清单，还是一份可直接审阅的文稿？
2. **做到哪里。** 可以读、可以整理、可以起草；发送、发布和花钱分别怎么批准？
3. **何时回来。** 按约定汇报进度；缺信息或超出范围时，带着问题来找我。

然后只交出去一件小事，连续观察一周。

看看它交付了什么，也看看自己少操了多少心。如果输出增加了三倍，检查与返工也增加了三倍，就还谈不上轻松。

## 05｜一人公司的机会，也许藏在“少挂念一件事”里

看到这些产品，我当然会兴奋。

过去很多想法做不下去，不一定是想法不好，而是一个人的时间被拆得太碎：刚进入创作状态，又要回复消息；刚准备做产品，又得找资料、整理表格。

如果 Agent 能稳定接住其中一小段，更多事情就可能有机会开始，也有机会做完。

但我不会因为一场发布会，就断言“一人公司已经全自动了”。

我更想看看：一个星期以后，原来拖着的事情有没有推进？人有没有多出一点完整的时间？晚上能不能少惦记几项待办？

这也是我对 AI 的期待：在创造之外，仍然有余力照顾身体、安顿情绪，去散步、去欣赏，去好好过一天。

**能把事情做完很重要。做完以后，人还能好好生活，同样重要。**

如果现在能交出去一件反复消耗你的事，你会先交哪件？

---

开放状态：截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日，Dots 在符合条件的市场向 Pro、Business Premium 用户分批开放；Enterprise（含 Edu、Healthcare）需管理员开启 beta。Muse 官方最新说明覆盖美国、加拿大。Cue 仍为邀请码早期体验；其发布公告称 iOS 将在 App Store 审核通过后陆续推出。各项功能与账号可用性以官方最新状态为准。[1][4][5]

配图取意于「虾子曰艺术风格图鉴」推荐的 **Rococo／洛可可风格**。用轻盈的曲线与柔和的光，画一点技术之外的生活想象。图像为 AI 创作的概念插画，不是产品界面。

本文依据官方发布材料讨论产品重心，未进行三款产品的同场实测。反馈整理场景为作者设想的试用任务；关于个人工作和一人公司的判断为作者观点。

资料与延伸阅读：

2. OpenAI｜GPT-6 Astra System Card，12.1 Dots：https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-astra/evaluating-auto-review
3. Meta｜Introducing Muse：https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/
4. Meta｜Muse for Small Business：https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/
5. Manus｜Manus 2.0 正式发布：https://manus.im/zh-cn/blog/introducing-manus-2-0
6. OpenAI｜Dots privacy, security, and safety FAQs：https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001529-dots-privacy-security-and-safety-faqs
7. OpenAI｜GPT-6 模型家族使用指南：https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model

en.label: FIELD NOTES
en.title: OpenAI Dots Is Here: As AI Gets More Capable, Can I Worry Less?
en.excerpt: What creates relief is not simply AI doing more, but an agent that can carry work forward, respect boundaries, and truly take one recurring responsibility off your mind.
en.content:
![OpenAI Dots, GPT-6.1 Sol, and a changing way of working with agents](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/source-poster.png)

Have you noticed that working with AI can feel like managing a remarkably capable colleague who still needs to be told “continue” every few minutes?

The plan is excellent. What happens next? You handle it.

The research is extensive. Who decides which source to trust? You do.

The task stops halfway through. Who remembers to resume it tomorrow? Still you.

By the end of the day, you have more content, more windows, and more unfinished tasks. You wanted an assistant. Instead, you gave yourself a new job: AI project manager.

Today I saw a poster about OpenAI Dots on Xiazi Daily’s “Yesterday’s World,” then followed its sources into the official materials. The question I care about most is whether it can reduce this kind of mental overhead.

**Can I hand off a piece of work and reclaim a little of my time as well?**

![AI is becoming more capable. Can I worry less?](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/cover.png)

## 01｜Dots Wants to Take the Whole Chain That Comes After the Prompt

Dots, introduced by OpenAI at DevDay, is an agent designed to keep working over time. OpenAI describes it as able to handle long-running tasks and continue making progress between conversations.[1]

You give it an objective, explain how far it may proceed on its own, and return later to review the result.

Several pieces support that continuity: its own cloud computer and browser, connected tools, persistent context, and the ability to delegate work to other agents.[1][2] OpenAI’s system card states that Dots is powered by GPT-6 Astra.[2]

The GPT-6.1 Sol shown in the same poster is a separate model update.[7] It helps to keep two developments distinct: model capability is improving, and the way we organize work around models is changing too.

Think about an ordinary day for an internet professional: review user feedback in the morning, revise the product at noon, inspect data in the afternoon, and prepare content at night. AI can help with each task in isolation. But the person still has to connect them into a project that actually moves forward.

That connective tissue is where Dots becomes interesting.

Can it remember where the work stopped? Can it adjust when the situation changes? When a branch requires human judgment, can it return with clear options rather than a vague problem?

> **Solving one problem is impressive. Carrying one piece of work forward reliably is what creates trust.**

![From answering once to carrying a piece of work forward](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/ongoing-work.png)

## 02｜I Would Rather Test It on a Small, Persistent Task

Consider user-feedback triage, one of the easiest responsibilities to postpone when you build an app alone.

You can already ask AI to “analyze this feedback” and receive something that resembles a consulting report. You read it, nod, close it, and never open it again.

I would rather try a delegation like this:

> For the next seven days, check the feedback sheet I authorize each day. Group repeated issues and preserve the original comments and sources. On Friday, deliver the three problems most worth fixing and explain why. Read and organize only: do not contact users or change the live product. Mark anything for which the evidence is insufficient.

This is a trial task I have designed, not a report of hands-on results with Dots.

Its value would be easy to inspect. Did something arrive on Friday? Are the sources correct? Did it correct yesterday’s misclassification today?

The savings may be more than twenty minutes of spreadsheet work. They may include the moment in the shower when you suddenly remember, “I still haven’t looked at that feedback.”

**For some work, the most exhausting part is keeping it alive in your head.**

For someone building products alone, reliably handing off one recurring responsibility is already valuable. There is no need to ask AI to run the whole company on day one.

## 03｜How Is It Different from Muse and Cue?

One misunderstanding is worth clearing up first: persistent execution is not unique to Dots.

Meta’s official introduction to Muse also emphasizes continuing after the app is closed, remembering long-term goals, and working across applications.[3]

All three products are moving toward the same broad direction: carrying work forward. The comparison below reflects the product emphasis I found in official materials. It is not a side-by-side benchmark.

![Three different product emphases, one shared direction: keep the work moving](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/three-agents.png)

**Dots: persistent delegation inside ChatGPT.**

It keeps conversation, connected work materials, and follow-up tasks in one relationship. I would first use it for work that needs several days of progress and repeated checks, then observe how many reminders I no longer have to send.

**Muse: moving from personal life into small business.**

On September 29, Meta introduced Muse for Small Business, connecting Shopify, Stripe, Slack, Notion, and Facebook and Instagram business accounts to help analyze operations and prepare marketing material. It is no longer only a personal assistant that helps plan a trip.[4]

My reading is that Muse is trying to support people who already run shops and business accounts: you attend to the customer in front of you while AI handles part of the work behind the counter.

**Cue: giving an agent an identity for dealing with the outside world.**

Manus highlights an agent’s own email address, phone number, wallet, and computer, along with group conversations in which several agents can collaborate. Payments remain constrained by the budget you set; the wallet should not be read as an unrestricted bank account.[5]

One concrete difference is that Dots’ launch documentation says it can connect to your personal email, but for now it cannot have an independent email address of its own or proactively call you. Cue places independent identity at the center of its proposition.[1]

Dots makes me think of persistent follow-up. Muse makes me think of an existing business. Cue makes me think of outward coordination.

Their capabilities overlap. The right choice still depends on your task, tools, and authorization model.

## 04｜Beyond Capability, I Care Whether It Knows When to Stop

Imagine asking, “Help me think about next week’s promotion,” only to discover that the AI has published ads, contacted customers, and spent the budget.

Very capable. Also very good for raising your blood pressure.

That is why one distinction in OpenAI’s explanation of Dots stood out to me: proactive research and authorized action are not the same thing.

OpenAI says proactive research can read permitted sources and organize information, but those research tools cannot directly send messages, modify content inside plugins, or control the computer. Later actions still have to follow permission and review. Sensitive steps such as money transfers require a person to take over, and not every completed action can be reversed.[6]

Meta is equally direct about Muse for Small Business: publishing, sending, and spending require user approval.[4]

These details will determine whether we trust agents in real work.

A good assistant should know what it may continue and what must wait. If you change your mind halfway through, it needs to hear you. If it becomes blocked, it needs to explain exactly where and why.

> **It should know when to continue—and when to stop.**

![Define the deliverable, permission boundary, and moment to report back](/assets/notes/2026-09-30-openai-dots/boundaries.png)

If I were preparing a first trial with Dots, I would write down three things:

1. **What to deliver.** A sourced list of candidates, or a draft ready for review?
2. **How far to go.** It may read, organize, and draft; how are sending, publishing, and spending approved?
3. **When to return.** Report on the agreed schedule, and come back with a question when information is missing or the task exceeds its scope.

Then I would delegate one small recurring responsibility and watch it for a week.

I would inspect what it delivered, and also how much mental load disappeared. If output triples while review and rework triple as well, life has not become lighter yet.

## 05｜The Opportunity for a One-Person Company May Be One Less Thing to Carry

Products like these excite me.

Many ideas fail to continue not because they are bad, but because one person’s time is fragmented. The moment you enter a creative rhythm, a message needs a reply. The moment you begin building the product, research and spreadsheets pull you away.

If an agent can reliably hold even one small part of that work, more projects may have a chance to begin—and to finish.

But I would not declare that one-person companies have become fully autonomous because of a launch event.

I would rather look a week later. Did the neglected task move forward? Did the person regain a block of uninterrupted time? Were there fewer unfinished items to remember at night?

That is also what I want from AI: enough energy left after creating to care for the body, settle the mind, take a walk, appreciate something beautiful, and live the day well.

**Finishing the work matters. Being able to live well after the work is finished matters too.**

If you could hand off one recurring responsibility that keeps draining you, which would you choose first?

---

Availability note: as of September 30, 2026, Dots was rolling out in eligible markets to Pro and Business Premium users; Enterprise, including Edu and Healthcare, required an administrator to enable the beta. Meta’s latest Muse information covered the United States and Canada. Cue remained in invitation-only early access, and its announcement said iOS would roll out after App Store review. Capabilities and account availability may continue to change.[1][4][5]

The illustrations draw on the Rococo style recommended by Xiazi Style Atlas: light curves and soft illumination create a little space for life beyond the technology. These are AI-generated concept illustrations, not product interfaces.

This article discusses product emphasis based on official launch materials. It is not a side-by-side test of all three products. The feedback-triage scenario is a proposed trial task, while the conclusions about personal work and one-person companies are the author’s interpretation.

Sources and further reading:

3. Meta, “Introducing Muse”: https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/
4. Meta, “Muse for Small Business”: https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/
5. Manus, “Introducing Manus 2.0”: https://manus.im/zh-cn/blog/introducing-manus-2-0
